request.spec:
When a claim is opened it receives the next number on the sheet: 1 for the first claim ever
opened on the sheet, then 2, and so on, with no gaps and never reused, even when two users open
claims at the same moment. A draft has no number, and voiding a claim clears its number (the
number is not given to anyone else). Show the number on the claim. Every audit line about a
claim that has a number gains number=<number> at its end (so CLAIM_OPENED and CLAIM_SETTLED
carry it; a CLAIM_VOIDED line carries the number the claim had).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit

AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Claims now get a number when they're opened, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass, including the one where two users open claims at the same moment.

- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V6__claim_number.sql`, adds a `claim_number` column to claims and a per-sheet counter, `last_claim_number`, to the sheet table.
- **Getting the number:** `Sheets.nextClaimNumber` adds one to the sheet's counter and reads it back within the open's own transaction. That locks the sheet's row until the open finishes, so two users opening claims at once get different numbers. If an open is refused, the counter change is undone too, so no number is skipped.
- **Open and void:** `ApplyClaimStatus` gives the claim its number on open and clears it on void. Before clearing, it passes the claim's number on as a `ClaimNumber` value, so `AuditClaimStatus` can still put it on the `CLAIM_VOIDED` line. That number is never given to another claim.
- **Audit lines:** every claim audit line now ends with ` number=<n>` when the claim has a number, and gets nothing extra when it doesn't. So `CLAIM_ADDED` lines and drafts (including voiding a draft) are unchanged.
- **Screen:** the claim response includes `number`, which is `""` when there is none, and each claim row shows it in `claim-number`.

The tests never void an opened claim, so the `CLAIM_VOIDED … number=<n>` line is implemented but not checked by them. They only void drafts, which correctly get no number.
